summary: Adds three endpoints: a user search by name, a per-key request counter guarded by a mutex, and an upstream status probe. It also wires them into the mux in main.go.

findings.title: Search query built from request input
findings.problem: Search pastes the name query parameter into the SQL text with fmt.Sprintf. A quote in name ends the string literal and lets the caller append arbitrary SQL.
findings.consequence: Any caller of GET /users can read or change every row in the database.
findings.fix: Use a placeholder in the query and pass name to QueryContext as a bound argument.
findings.suggested_change: rows, err := h.DB.QueryContext(r.Context(), "SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE name = ?", name)

findings.title: Mutex left locked on missing key
findings.problem: Count locks h.mu before it checks the key. It then returns on an empty key without unlocking.
findings.consequence: One request to GET /count without a key blocks every later Count request forever. Each blocked request also leaks a goroutine.
findings.fix: Validate the key before calling h.mu.Lock. Another option is to call defer h.mu.Unlock right after the lock.

findings.title: Response body closed before error check
findings.problem: fetchStatus defers resp.Body.Close before it checks err. When http.Get fails, resp is nil, so the deferred call panics.
findings.consequence: An unreachable upstream makes GET /upstream panic and drop the connection. The client never gets the intended 502 response.
findings.fix: Check err first and return on failure. Defer resp.Body.Close only after that check.

findings.title: New handlers have no covering test
findings.problem: The change adds the Search, Count and Upstream handlers without any test. The repository contains no _test.go files.
findings.consequence: Nothing catches regressions such as the lock leak or the nil response panic in these handlers.
findings.fix: Add httptest-based tests for each handler, including the missing key and unreachable upstream paths.

dropped.reason: This flags the same Sprintf query that the c1 finding already covers. Raising it again would duplicate one problem.
